caption_hook: Utah has been a tropical sea, a vast desert and a lake so big it covered a third of the state.

layers.name: CLARON FORMATION
layers.what: Rivers and shallow lakes laid down pink and orange limestone and mud. Frost and rain then carved the edge of the plateau into thousands of spires called hoodoos.
layers.bonus: Bryce Canyon holds the world's largest collection of hoodoos.

layers.name: ENTRADA SANDSTONE
layers.what: Coastal dunes and sandy flats near an inland sea hardened into red and orange sandstone. Wind and water carved it into arches, fins and balanced rocks.
layers.bonus: Delicate Arch and more than 2,000 other arches in Arches National Park are mostly this rock.

layers.name: NAVAJO SANDSTONE
layers.what: Towering dunes drifted across western North America. Today the cliffs show their curved, slanted layers, frozen mid-drift in the stone, in places hundreds of feet thick.
layers.bonus: Zion's 2,000-foot walls are mostly Navajo Sandstone, and its dunes once covered much of the West.

layers.name: CEDAR MESA SANDSTONE
layers.hook: Striped spires of an older desert
layers.what: Before the dinosaurs, coastal dunes and beaches built layer after layer of sand. Cracks and weathering now cut it into the red-and-white-striped pillars of the Needles.
layers.bonus: The Needles District of Canyonlands is carved from it, and the spires look like giant striped candy.

layers.name: WHEELER SHALE
layers.hook: Trilobites in a Utah sea bed
layers.what: A warm Cambrian sea covered western Utah, and mud buried trilobites so quickly that even soft body parts sometimes survived. The fossils sit in the House Range.
layers.bonus: Anyone can dig trilobites here at public quarries near Delta.

layers.name: FARMINGTON CANYON
layers.what: Banded gneiss and schist, once buried deep in the crust and baked under great heat and pressure, form the core of the Wasatch Range and Antelope Island.
layers.bonus: Antelope Island sits in the Great Salt Lake, which is salty because it has no outlet.
